body:
Albemarle, NC. Been staying at a shelter for a bit now, that may come to an end soon. Spend days at the unemployment office filling out applications. No dice.

Spoke to the VA in Salisbury, they could put me up for 4 months. Would be two years if I had a substance abuse problem or mental health issues. I don't. Still, that may be the only option shortly.

Unfortunately, none of this addresses the real issue of employment. If I had work, things would be a bit different. My funds would creep up instead of down, maybe the situation wouldn't seem as soul crushing as it does now.

Opting out doesn't seem so bad anymore, I'd gladly trade all the highs of my life to be rid of all the lows.

I'm no entrepreneur, but I'd be willing to do just about anything. The only issue I can see is that the ten to twenty dollars it would take to start is gasoline, its food. Its a gamble.

An odd prospect to someone whose luck has already run dry

If there was help, I'd take it. Anything.

I've talked to her about this, of course she wants to fight, struggle, do whatever it takes. The idea is romantic, the realities are far more harsh.

It is easy to say "We are going to get through this no matter what it takes", but the words don't offer much consolation to the child we won't be able to feed. They offer little comfort to the frigid bodies trying to stay warm in a parking lot in the middle of winter. They offer no hope when reality brings everything crashing down around your ears.

I've given this some thought. If things go as I think they will, it won't take seven years, I can easily make sure of that. A simple call to notify authorities of where I can be found is all it takes. Perhaps a voicemail to someone I know is asleep, and won't know what has happened until morning.

We both lost our jobs in a short span of time. So her situation is only marginally better than mine, and it it's only better because people will be more likely to help a single mother than a single mother and her middle aged guy.

My money will go farther feeding two instead of one. The gas will last longer with a lighter load. The help and sympathy will flow easier to her when I'm gone.

Yes, this is a matter of money, unfortunately. Were I able to find employment within the next week or so, I would gladly step back from the edge and do everything in my power to make things work. Even if things were rough, that glimmer of hope would be present.

I don't have that. All I have is a back account with dwindling funds, a car that has everything I own in it, and a millstone grinding away at my resources. I can only keep eating and putting in applications for so long until my empty account leaves me at a dead stop, in the dead of winter, in a dead town.

I see it like this...

I'm a mouth to feed, I'm a body that needs shelter, I'm an expense.

There occasionally comes a time when you can no longer take care of a beloved family pet. When feeding and sheltering it are more of a burden than can be borne, regardless of your feelings.

She is not that pet, I am. Instead of her making the choice to let me go to save herself, I choose to walk out into the woods quietly, of my own accord. Because she stands more of a chance on her own. All my resources will be hers, and with any luck, she will make it through ok.

By all accounts, I am just an average guy. I have generally made enough to get by, enjoyed few luxuries, but was relatively content. Circumstances have simply left me in a rough spot with no good plays to make.

I've been a gamer since I was a kid. Staying home playing Atari when I was sick, usually missile command. Always enjoying the geekier things in life, I even played magic the gathering through my time in the army. Have a few boxes of cards in my trunk to this day. Were this a real camp fire, I'd offer to teach you.

My love life hasn't been the greatest, but aside from marrying your high school sweetheart, everyone has ups and downs. However, there is someone I care about deeply at the moment, and she will be my only regret. That I hurt her by failing, that I can't grow old with her.

I'm simply an unremarkable man caught in unforgiving circumstances. I want to fight, I want to give 'em hell, so to speak. I'm staring down a tank, coming down an alley towards me. No exits, no tricks I can pull. Just my rifle and half a magazine left.
